subject: Pre-sales dedicated fleet questionnaire: traffic & prompt profile for sizing
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda@cloudflow.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: sales_ops@cloudflow.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - CloudFlow

Hi Dev,

Thanks for offering to help size a dedicated pool for us. We're evaluating a Dedicated deployment and want a realistic sizing estimate (GPUs, burst capacity, expected concurrency). Attached is a small sample of real queries (cloudflow-sample-queries.jsonl) and a brief questionnaire we filled out. High level:

- Expected steady-state QPS: 30 requests/sec
- Typical request type: single-turn instruction completion (user prompt -> model reply)
- Weighted prompt length: 180 tokens (median), 450 tokens (95th)
- Weighted response length: 120 tokens (median), 600 tokens (95th)
- Peak window: 3x steady (90 req/s) for ~10 minutes, ~2x for sustained daily bursts (2 hours)
- SLA requirement: p95 latency < 350ms for streaming start / total completion < 1.2s where possible

Can you confirm what information you need to give us an initial GPU-compute recommendation (types & counts) and an order-of-magnitude cost delta for Dedicated vs hosted? We're targeting live POC in ~6 weeks if sizing looks good.

Thanks,
Amanda Li
Director of Platform 
CloudFlow AI

Attachments: cloudflow-sample-queries.jsonl (3.4 MB)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@cloudflow.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - CloudFlow

Hi Amanda —

Thanks for the sample and the profile; this is a great start. A few clarifying questions so our sizing calc lines up with your traffic patterns:

1) Model family and precision: which model(s) are you planning to serve (open Llama-style 70B, or a smaller 13B, or a commercial variant)? Also whether you plan to use fp16, int8, or a quantized variant matters for capacity.

2) Streaming vs non-streaming: do you expect the clients to stream token-by-token (we treat streaming differently for warmed KV cache and CPU overhead)? If streaming, what is your target initial-token latency vs completion?

3) Concurrency distribution: you gave steady 30 r/s and 90 r/s peak window. Can you share expected per-user concurrency (e.g., mostly 1 request at a time per user) and whether those peaks are bursty (all at once) or spread over regionally phased users?

4) Warm cache opportunities: do you expect many repeated prefixes or templates we can exploit for prefix caching? If yes, what pct of requests are highly templated (e.g., system prompts + user prompt structure)?

5) Availability & fallbacks: what's your acceptable failure mode? Do you need 99.9% throughput SLAs on dedicated pool even under infra maintenance, or is a best-effort with fallback to hosted acceptable?

If you prefer, we can do a 30–45 minute call and walk through the attached sample together; Marissa can run a quick throughput run to estimate GPU hours.

I'll drop a first-pass calc after you confirm model choices & streaming preference.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Amanda Li <amanda@cloudflow.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: sales_ops@cloudflow.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - CloudFlow

Hi Dev —

Answers inline below. Happy to jump on a call if that helps.

1) Model family: currently planning to use an open 34B variant for the POC with a plan to evaluate 70B for higher-tier customers later. We'll start with fp16 and may test int8 quantization.

2) Streaming: yes, clients use streaming for chat UI. Primary metric is initial token start within 200–300ms; full completion timing is less strict but we prefer under 1.5s for median flows.

3) Concurrency distribution: mostly single-request-per-user; our web frontend tends to fan out to 1–3 concurrent requests for background relevance checks. Peaks are regionally correlated - most traffic comes from NA with a smaller EU footprint. Peaks are short but sharp (all-at-once on localized events).

4) Warm cache: ~40% of requests use templated prompts (e.g., system + user template); the remainder are open questions.

5) Availability: for the POC we can accept best-effort with automatic fallback to hosted. For production we will require an SLA conversation.

Thanks — I'll attach a CSV with a 48-hour request histogram if that helps.

— Amanda

Attachments: cloudflow-48h-histogram.csv (120 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - CloudFlow

Thanks for the clarifications. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the sample and Amanda's answers; logging it here so Aisha and I can align before we send a formal recommendation.

Summary of assumptions:
- Model: 34B, fp16 runtime profile (KV-cache warm start for templated prompts)
- Median tokens per request: prompt 180 + response 120 = 300 total; p95 = 1050 total
- Steady-state: 30 requests/s; steady token rate median ≈ 9k tokens/s; p95 token bursts ≈ 31.5k tokens/s (90 req/s * 350 median tokens)
- Latency SLO: p95 start <350ms, completion <1.2–1.5s for median lengths

Sizing calc (first-pass):
- For 34B fp16, observed throughput on A100-80GB equivalent per GPU (continuous, non-streaming ideal) is ~12–16 median requests/s (300 tokens median) depending on batching. With streaming overhead and real-world variance, use conservative 10 median req/s per A100.
- To cover steady 30 req/s: 3x A100 with smart batching and caching (headroom for autoscaling to handle short bursts).
- Peak window (90 req/s for 10 minutes): requires ~9 A100 if we wanted to handle fully in-pool without queueing; but we can achieve the peak with 4–5 A100 + short-lived burst capacity (pre-warmed on Dedicated or fallback to hosted).
- Cost tradeoff: Dedicated pool (3–5 A100 baseline with burst to 9) will be ~2.2–3.5x the hosted list compute cost for steady usage but gives predictable latency and isolation. Exact numbers depend on committed hours and region.

Recommendations for POC:
1) Baseline Dedicated pool: 3x A100-80GB (fp16) with autoscaler that can add 2–6 GPUs for bursts; configure prefix caching for templated prompts to reduce p95 pressure.
2) Enable a hybrid fallback policy: overflow-to-hosted for sudden spikes above burst capacity and a canary routing rule for the first 24 hours of POC traffic changes.
3) Performance ops: pre-warm KV caches for expected templates, pin model variant, and run a synthetic throughput test (Marissa can perform) to validate p95.

I'll package this into the sizing worksheet and include per-GPU cost estimates; want to loop Aisha for pricing approval before sending to Amanda.

— Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Amanda Li <amanda@cloudflow.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Best,
